successCriteria.description: mapRow returns beforeState/afterState as parsed values (objects/arrays/primitives), not the raw JSON string, whenever the corresponding before_state/after_state column is non-null.
A null before_state or after_state column maps to null (JSON.parse is never invoked on null), preserving the AuditLog `unknown | null` contract.
Round-trip symmetry: a value passed to create() (which JSON.stringify's it) is returned by findById() as a structurally equal value after mapRow parses it back.

constraints: JSON.parse must be guarded so it is only invoked when the column value is non-null; null columns must map to null without parsing.
The write path is unchanged: create() continues to JSON.stringify non-null beforeState/afterState before insert; this phase only alters the read/mapping path.
No `any` may be introduced; parsed values remain typed `unknown` (per the HARNESS no-any rule and the existing AuditLog model).
outOfScope: Changing the write path (create()'s JSON.stringify), the AuditLog model shape, the repository interface, or adding routes/controllers/RBAC — none of these are part of this phase.

ambiguities.description: Behavior when a non-null before_state/after_state column contains malformed JSON (JSON.parse throws).
options: Return the raw string unchanged on parse failure

entityInvariants.invariant: beforeState and afterState remain `unknown | null`; after mapping, a non-null column yields the parsed value and a null column yields null.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The mapped AuditLog must satisfy the AuditLog interface declared in audit.model.ts (beforeState/afterState: unknown | null), and the parse must be the inverse of the JSON.stringify performed in create() so round-trips are lossless.
The parse behavior must be the exact inverse of the existing JSON.stringify in create() within audit.repository.ts, so values written by create() are returned structurally equal by findById().
